summary_html: A **judge orders** CPS to investigate or assess during civil/criminal proceedings. Federal funding statutes (ASFA/IV-E) tether court findings to child-welfare actions, embedding judicial oversight into intake-to-case flow.
authority_html:
- **ASFA (42 U.S.C. §§ 671–675)** — court ‘reasonable efforts’ findings; permanency timelines  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funding structure linking court oversight to agency actions

primary_citations.citation_text: New Mexico - NMSA 1978 Chapter 32A, Article 4 (Abuse and Neglect Act: 32A-4-3 duty to report, 32A-4-18 custody hearings, 32A-4-19 adjudicatory hearings), CYFD-published Children's Code compilation (2023 text; 32A-4-3 amended 2025 by SB 42)

New Mexico Statutes Chapter 27 - Public Assistance (public assistance and Medicaid programs; CYFD's child-welfare authority is not in this chapter — it is the Children, Youth and Families Department Act, NMSA 1978 § 9-2A-7(D), and the Children's Code, NMSA 1978 § 32A-1-1, per 8.10.3.3 NMAC)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Children, Youth & Families Department v. Calvin T.
key_cases.holding: The Court held that a children's court may join 'any other person' under Rule 10-121(B)(4) NMRA only where that person is a necessary party under the Rule 1-019(A)(1) standard, and remanded for the children's court to apply that standard to the youth's managed care organization.
key_cases.relevance: It shows the children's court exercising its own authority to pull additional entities into an abuse and neglect case to obtain services for the child.
key_cases.quote: the set of parties necessary to afford complete relief sought in such proceedings will include those parties necessary to serve the best interests of the child

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Children, Youth & Families Department v. Mercer-Smith
key_cases.holding: The Court held that the purpose for which the district court exercised its contempt power against CYFD was not remedial and therefore could not be sustained as civil contempt, and it reversed the contempt order and vacated the nearly four-million-dollar award in its entirety.
key_cases.relevance: It arose from a judicial placement order directed at CYFD and shows how far a court may go in enforcing such an order.
key_cases.quote: we reverse the contempt order and vacate the award in its entirety

mandatory_reporters: Licensed physicians, residents and interns examining, attending or treating a child (named in the statute as examples, not limits)
School employees (includes employees of a school district or a public school)
Social workers acting in an official capacity
Clergy, as to information that is not privileged as a matter of law
reporting_details: In New Mexico every person who knows or has a reasonable suspicion that a child is abused or neglected must report it immediately to a local law enforcement agency, to CYFD (Statewide Central Intake, 1-855-333-7233), or, for an Indian child residing in Indian country, to a tribal law enforcement or social services agency, and failing to report is a misdemeanor (NMSA 1978 § 32A-4-3(A), (F)). A finding that a pregnant woman is using or abusing drugs, made pursuant to an interview, self-report, clinical observation or routine toxicology screen, does not alone form a sufficient basis to report child abuse or neglect, and a volunteer, contractor or staff member of a hospital or freestanding birthing center shall not make a report based solely on that finding; notification of a plan of safe care goes to the health care authority and is not a report of abuse or neglect (NMSA 1978 § 32A-4-3(G)–(I), as amended by Laws 2025, ch. 156).
